correctness.rationale: With u=theta x and a=1/(1+theta), the original modified-Lindley baseline has s0=e^(−u)(1+a u e^(−u)) and f0=theta e^(−u)[1+a(2u−1)e^(−u)]. It follows exactly that h0/theta=[1+a(2u−1)e^(−u)]/[1+a u e^(−u)]=1+a(u−1)e^(−u)+O(u²e^(−2u)). Raising the baseline CDF to alpha>0 multiplies h0 by M_alpha(s0)=alpha s0 (1−s0)^(alpha−1)/[1−(1−s0)^alpha]=1−(alpha−1)s0/2+O(s0²). Thus h/theta=1+[a(u−1)−(alpha−1)/2]e^(−u)+O(u²e^(−2u)) and the explicitly differentiated exact analytic formula gives d(h/theta)/du=[a(2−u)+(alpha−1)/2]e^(−u)+O(u²e^(−2u)). Since the u e^(−u) term dominates, h approaches theta FROM ABOVE and h′<0 eventually for every theta,alpha>0. The two scaled limits are theta/(1+theta) and −theta²/(1+theta). At alpha>1, the small-x hazard behaves as const*x^(alpha−1), giving increasing hazard near x=0; at alpha=1, h′(0+)=theta²(2theta+3)/(1+theta)²>0. Thus alpha>=1 has at least one interior local maximum. Independent high-precision 70-digit direct evaluation at u=25,35 for three parameter pairs confirmed exact normalized correction and strictly negative far-tail derivative; numerical tests are not the proof of eventuality.
residual_risks: No uniqueness of hazard peak is proved; alpha<1 nearzero hazard may diverge and intermediate extrema are unclassified.
The first-order asymptotic alone does not provide the smallest finite sign-change time.
The analytic derivative expansion is justified by the exact expression, not by blindly differentiating a bare big-O term.
